title: Corn Tortilla Taco with Pork, Beans and Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: A corn tortilla taco filled with pork, beans and cheese is a classic Mexican dish. The thin corn tortilla is lightly toasted, while the juicy pork, seasoned beans and melted cheese create a balanced, flavorful bite.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Corn tortillas have been used in Mexico for over 7,000 years.
Pork for tacos is often marinated in a blend of chili, lime and spices for a distinctive aroma.
Beans are a traditional source of plant protein in Mexican cuisine, commonly served as refried beans.
Cheese used in tacos is often queso fresco or melted cheddar.
Traditional serving method is to fold the tortilla in half and eat it by hand.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Pork and beans provide high‑quality protein essential for tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Beans contain soluble and insoluble fiber that supports healthy digestion.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Pork supplies vitamin B12, while beans are a good source of folate, both important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: Corn tortilla and beans deliver iron, magnesium and potassium.

items.title: Low glycemic index
items.content: Corn tortillas have a lower glycemic index than wheat flour tortillas, helping to moderate blood sugar spikes.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to corn products, including tortillas.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Cheese and sauces can increase sodium intake, which should be monitored by people with hypertension.

items.title: Fat content of meat
items.content: Pork can contain saturated fats; choosing lean cuts or trimming excess fat is recommended.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Traditional tacos are calorie‑dense; portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Hold the taco in one hand, folding the tortilla in half. Add fresh toppings such as diced tomatoes, onion, cilantro and a squeeze of lime for extra brightness. Serve with salsa, guacamole or sour cream if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store prepared tacos in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Keep tortillas in a dry place; if they become soft, briefly warm them on a dry skillet before serving.
